title: Error of a sparse Fourier approximation
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite family of subsets of $[n]$, and let $c$ assign a real coefficient to each subset of $[n]$. The squared uniform $2$-norm of the difference between $f$ and the approximation $x\mapsto\sum_{S\in\mathcal{F}}c(S)\chi_S(x)$ equals $\sum_{S\in\mathcal{F}}(\widehat f(S)-c(S))^2+\sum_{S\notin\mathcal{F}}\widehat f(S)^2$, where $\widehat f(S)$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ and $\chi_S$ is the corresponding Boolean-cube character.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathcal{F}$ is a finite family of subsets of $[n]$
$c$ is a real-valued coefficient function on the subsets of $[n]$
